description:
Searches a database for real-time job listings matching the user's criteria.

The query is the full job title or role: "Ruby Developer" rather than
a bare keyword like "Ruby", which is too broad and matches unrelated fields. roles_lookup turns
words that name no exact role into FoundRole roles with their job counts. Results may be
filtered by location, company, and how recently a job was posted.

Each result carries an `id` and `resultItemId`; jobs_details takes that `id` with the corresponding
`result_item_id` and returns the job's full description, requirements, and benefits. One call returns one answer: there is no next page, and the
response links to the same search on the FoundRole website for the rest of the list.

With a ready profile, a query for the profile's target profession or an omitted query uses the same
personalized feed as jobs_recommendations and the website; alternative titles of that same role
return that same feed. An account's saved role is reported in every response as savedRole; an
omitted query or the saved role's title searches exactly that role. A different or unrecognized
profession uses general job search, preserving the explicit query and filters, and leaves the saved
role unchanged. A search without a location runs in the place saved on the account, widened to its
country when few jobs are posted near that city; an account with no saved place searches where the
user is now when the client reports it, otherwise the default country. Such a response names the place
searched as searchedPlace. A response for a request that names no exact role can carry a guide
question the widget shows to the user. Job details include
FoundRole salary benchmarks, H-1B sponsorship signals, E-Verify status, and job-trust analysis;
list-level employer signals follow the user's current entitlements.

Constraints in the user's request — remote-only work, H1B sponsorship, a minimum salary,
a minimum match grade — are the search parameters remote, h1b_sponsors_only,
salary_floor, and min_match; sort orders the results by relevance, newest, salary
or personal match. The search enforces only constraints passed as parameters; a constraint left out
of the call is not applied to the result set.

Job type, work mode, required education, experience level, benefits, bonuses, employers to include or
exclude, and the search radius are the parameters employment_types, work_modes, education,
experience_levels, benefits, bonuses_only, companies, exclude_companies and radius. Remote and hybrid
are independent work modes: a remote search never returns hybrid jobs. A job that does not state the
filtered attribute is left out while that filter is set. One brand inside a company is hiring_brand
next to company.

A company name that several employers share covers all of them, and the response names each with its
domain; an employer's domain in place of a name (company, companies or exclude_companies) means that
employer alone.

When nothing matches, a city search is repeated within 100 miles and the
response says so; a search limited by posted_days_ago keeps that limit and reports how many jobs match over a
longer period instead of listing them.

Advanced filters (sort, min_match, h1b_sponsors_only, salary_floor, remote, work_modes, benefits, bonuses_only, companies, exclude_companies; sort only when ordering by salary or match, companies only
when it names more than one employer) apply for every account. One answer lists the first
matching jobs and states how many further jobs match.

benefits.description: Advanced filter: benefit names such as "health insurance", "401k" or "parental leave"; a job qualifies only when it states every listed benefit. Names that match no known benefit are ignored.

bonuses_only.description: Advanced filter: only jobs that state a bonus (sign-on, performance, referral, commission and the like).

companies.description: Filter: official company names; a job from any of them qualifies, across every job board each employer posts on. More than one company makes it an advanced filter. Next to company, a job has to match both; hiring_brand narrows company only.

company.description: The official company name, or the domain of one employer

education.description: Filter: jobs whose posting requires one of these education levels (no_requirements, high_school, associate_degree, bachelor_degree, professional_certificate, postgraduate_degree); bachelor_degree means the posting asks for a bachelor degree, not that it suits someone holding one.

employment_types.description: Filter: jobs offered as any of these employment types (full_time, part_time, contractor, temporary, intern, volunteer, per_diem, other).

exclude_companies.description: Advanced filter: official company names whose jobs are removed from the results, across every job board each employer posts on.

experience_levels.description: Filter: jobs at any of these experience levels (entry_level, mid_level, senior_level, executive, level_not_stated). The level comes from the years of experience the posting asks for and the seniority in its title, the higher of the two; entry_level never includes a posting asking for more than two years. level_not_stated selects jobs whose level cannot be derived; it can be selected alone or alongside other levels.

h1b_sponsors_only.description: Advanced filter: only companies known to sponsor H1B visas.

hiring_brand.description: Filter: one brand inside the company, for example company "Google" with hiring_brand "YouTube"; used only together with company.

min_match.description: Advanced filter: lowest personal FoundRole match grade to keep, the same letter each job shows in insights.match.grade. A and A- are rare even for a strong resume; B keeps good and strong matches; C+ also keeps fair ones. Needs a resume on the account.

posted_days_ago.description: Number of days ago to search for jobs (1-365)

query.description: The full job title or skill (e.g., "Ruby Developer", NOT just "Ruby")

radius.description: Search radius in miles around a city location (default 40); not used for state, country or remote searches.

remote.description: Advanced filter: only remote-eligible jobs, matched across the whole country of the requested location rather than its radius.

salary_floor.description: Advanced filter: minimum annualized salary in USD; a posting qualifies when the lower bound of its pay band reaches the floor. Jobs without a USD salary are dropped.

sort.description: Result order (score, posted_at, match, salary): score is relevance and the default, posted_at is newest first, salary is highest pay first, match is best personal fit first and needs a resume. Ordering by salary or match is an advanced option.

work_modes.description: Advanced filter: jobs in any of these work modes (on_site, remote, hybrid). remote is matched across the whole country of the location, the others within the radius. ["remote"] is the same search as remote: true.
